content.doc_md:
TheRIGHT JOINreturnsall rows from the right table(table2), and only the matched rows from the left table (table1).

If there is no match in the left table, the result for the columns from the left table will be NULL.

TheRIGHT JOINandRIGHT OUTER JOINkeywords are equal - theOUTERkeyword is optional.

Note:The syntax combines two tables based on arelated column, 
and theONkeyword is used to specify the matching condition.

Here we see that the related column between the two tables above, is the "EmployeeID" column.

The following SQL will return all employees, and any orders they might have placed:

Note:TheRIGHT JOINkeyword returns all records from the 
right table (Employees), even if there are no matches in the left table 
(Orders).

### Code Snippets

```
SELECT
column_name(s)
FROM
table1
RIGHT JOIN
table2
ON
table1.column_name
=
table2.column_name
;

---

SELECT Orders.OrderID, Employees.LastName, Employees.FirstName
FROM Orders
RIGHT JOIN Employees ON Orders.EmployeeID = Employees.EmployeeID
ORDER BY Orders.OrderID;
```
